name: One More Thing
description: Retrieval practice that's structurally social: everyone lists what they remember from memory, the list passes to two classmates who each add one thing it missed, and it returns to its author grown. Ends with the class's collective memory, AI-combined.
tagline: Perfect as an exit ticket, a unit review, or the first five minutes of the next day.

lesson.label: What are they remembering?
lesson.helper: Fills the prompts: 'today's lesson', 'chapter 7', 'the photosynthesis unit', 'yesterday's lab'.

recallTime.label: Recall time (seconds)
recallTime.helper: Time for the first from-memory list. The two add-one rounds get 90 seconds each.

template.name: One More Thing
template.description: A pass-and-add memory chain built with the One More Thing recipe, every list returns to its author grown.

intro.message:
ONE MORE THING

From memory, no notes! You'll list what you remember from ${lesson}. Then your list travels: two classmates will each add one thing you missed.

It comes back to you, grown.

recall.prompt: From memory (no notes!): list the 2-3 most important things you remember from ${lesson}. Put each on its own line.

add-one.prompt: A classmate's list is in the box below. Read it, then ADD one thing they missed, a detail, a missing point, or a connection between ideas. New line, leave their lines alone.

add-again.prompt: A different classmate's list, already grown once. Read the whole thing, then ADD one more thing it's still missing. New line.

cluster.instruction: These are memory lists about ${lesson}, each grown by three different students. Combine them into ONE master list of what the class collectively remembered: most-mentioned ideas first, grouped by theme, duplicates merged. End by naming one or two things that only a single list caught, credit the catch, not the student.

end.message: That's One More Thing, nobody's list came back the same size it left.
